license.note: Original Army Individual Test Battery (1944) format is in the public domain; widely reproduced in neuropsychology with attribution to Reitan (1958).

response_scale: Performance-based: completion time in seconds per part (A: 25 circles numbered 1-25; B: 25 circles alternating 1-13 numbers and A-L letters), clinician-administered

scoring.note: TMT-A score = completion time in seconds (max 180s for A); TMT-B = completion time (max 300s for B); errors add time per convention. The derived measure of interest is the B-A difference (or B/A ratio), indexing cognitive-flexibility/set-shifting demand beyond pure speed. Norms: age-, education-, and sometimes IQ-corrected percentile tables (Tombaugh 2004; Salthouse & Fristoe 1995). Higher time = worse performance.

cutoffs.interpretation: TMT-A >50s and TMT-B >120s are rough adult screening flags, but interpretation MUST use age/education-adjusted norm tables (Tombaugh 2004) — raw seconds alone are not diagnostic.

algorithm.B_A_difference: TMT-B seconds minus TMT-A seconds (set-shifting cost)

subscale_note: Part A (visual search/processing speed) and Part B (set-shifting) + B-A difference; performance test, not self-report.

license.note: Classic Stroop paradigm in the public domain; many published variants (Golden 1978; Trenerry et al. 1989 VST) — specific card sets may carry copyright.

response_scale: Performance-based: completion time in seconds + number of errors per condition (Word, Color, Color-Word interference)

scoring.note: Stroop: 3 conditions (Word naming, Color naming, Color-Word interference). Scores = completion time + errors per condition. The derived measure of interest is the INTERFERENCE score (Color-Word time minus expected non-interference time — e.g., Golden's predicted formula or the simple Color-Word minus Color difference), indexing inhibitory control. Norms: age- and education-corrected (Golden 1978; Strauss et al. 2006 compendium). Higher interference time = worse inhibitory control.

cutoffs.interpretation: Interference score interpreted against age/education-adjusted norms (Golden 1978; Strauss et al. 2006) — raw times alone are not diagnostic.

algorithm.interference_score: Color-Word time minus predicted non-interference time (Golden formula) or Color-Word minus Color

subscale_note: 3 conditions + interference score; performance test, not self-report.

Cutoffs (per subscale, doubled; Lovibond & Lovibond 1995 manual + Antony 1998): Depression normal 0-9, mild 10-13, moderate 14-20, severe 21-27, extremely severe 28+; Anxiety normal 0-7, mild 8-9, moderate 10-14, severe 15-19, extremely severe 20+; Stress normal 0-14, mild 15-18, moderate 19-25, severe 26-33, extremely severe 34+.

cutoffs.interpretation: DASS-21 reports 3 subscale scores (after x2 doubling), each banded separately: Depression 0-9/10-13/14-20/21-27/28+ (normal/mild/moderate/severe/extremely severe); Anxiety 0-7/8-9/10-14/15-19/20+; Stress 0-14/15-18/19-25/26-33/34+. See Lovibond & Lovibond (1995) manual Table 3.

Cutoffs (Clayton et al. 1997): total <=41 (men) / <=41 (women) indicates sexual dysfunction (sex-specific norms differ by version).

official_name: Portrait Values Questionnaire — Short Form (Schwartz Value Survey)

license.note: Free for research use with attribution (Schwartz 2006); ESS Human Values Scale variant also available.

response_scale: 1-6 per item (Very much like me → Not at all like me)

scoring.note: SVS (Schwartz Value Survey — the 21-item short form version referenced in the catalog as 'SVS'): 10 basic values arranged in the Schwartz circumplex (Self-Direction, Stimulation, Hedonism, Achievement, Power, Security, Conformity, Tradition, Benevolence, Universalism). Score = mean per value after ipsative centering (subtract the respondent's overall mean — values are compared RELATIVELY). Validation (Schwartz 2006): alphas .56-.75 (short form; modest). **Catalog lists VM01 (PVQ) and PP04 (SVS) as separate instruments — they may be the same scale family; verify whether the catalog intends two distinct value measures.**

subscale_note: 10 basic values in the Schwartz circumplex; values are compared RELATIVELY (ipsative), not absolutely.

response_scale: Mixed: items 1-5 anchors (poor-excellent health, frequency anchors), past 7 days

scoring.note: PROMIS Global Health (10 items): produces 2 summary scores — Global Physical Health (GPH, 3 items) and Global Mental Health (GMH, 4 items), plus a Global Health total. Scores are IRT-transformed to T-metrics (M = 50, SD = 10, US general population), often rescaled 0-100. Validation (Hays et al. 2010): alphas GPH .81, GMH .86. Cutoffs: T 50 = population mean; T >=60 commonly flagged as clinically elevated.

cutoffs.interpretation: Global health at/below 1 SD above the population mean (lower T = better for the negative-oriented scoring, depending on direction — verify scoring direction per healthmeasures.net)
1-2 SD above mean — clinically notable global health burden
2+ SD above mean — severe global health burden

algorithm.implementation: item-level lookup tables from healthmeasures.net scoring service

subscale_note: 2 summary scores (GPH, GMH) + total; provides a brief all-domain health snapshot.
